{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested:
#   -l nodes=64:ppn=16:xe
#   -q high
#   -l walltime=1:00:00
#   -N select_neurotrees
#   -e ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.err
#   -o ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.out
#   -W umask=0027
#   (email -m bea is commented out in the input)

# Request 64 nodes, 1024 total tasks (64*16).
flux alloc \
  -N 64 \
  -n 1024 \
  --time=1h \
  --queue=high \
  bash -lc '

# PBS umask
umask 0027

mkdir -p ./results

# Approximate PBS $PBS_JOBID naming using Flux job id.
exec >"./results/neurotrees_select.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"./results/neurotrees_select.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: PBS job name (-N select_neurotrees) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: PBS node property ":xe" (hardware type constraint) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: you may be scheduled on different node types (if available), affecting performance
# or compatibility.

module swap PrgEnv-cray PrgEnv-gnu
module load cray-hdf5-parallel

set -x

# PBS $PBS_O_WORKDIR: use current directory as a best-effort fallback if not set.
cd "${PBS_O_WORKDIR:-$PWD}"

# NOTE: PBS used aprun for Cray systems. Flux does not portably provide an aprun equivalent.
# Performance implication: if aprun is required to launch across nodes on your system, the job may fail to use
# all allocated resources or fail to start. If Flux is integrated with your MPI stack, replace aprun with
# a site-supported Flux launcher (e.g., flux run -n 1024 ...).

aprun -n 1024 ./build/neurotrees_select -p GC -i 256 --reindex \
      --cachesize=$((4 * 1024 * 1024)) \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_extended_20171019_compressed.h5 \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_reindex_20170615.dat \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_20171019.h5
'
"
}
